item.title: Data-driven geometric phase in biological locomotion
item.description: arXiv:2606.22440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometric phase quantifies net locomotion in dissipative media via gauge theory, but linking this theoretical quantity to noisy, sparse, and weakly periodic biological shape data is challenging. We develop a theory-guided, data-driven Koopman autoencoder to recover the limit cycle embedded in imperfect cyclic data and extract shape gaits and geometric phase from sperm and nematode data. We introduce a geometric phase sensitivity function that quantifies responses to shape perturbations and reveals mechanical information using only gauge-theoretic structure, without assuming mechanical laws.
item.dc:creator: Pyae Hein Htet, Kenta Ishimoto
